title: Microsoft Azure Administrator — expanded study guide

lessons.title: Introduction
points: Azure Cloud Shell provides an authenticated browser command line for managing Azure resources with Bash or PowerShell.

lessons.title: What is Azure Cloud Shell?
points: Cloud Shell lets you manage virtual machines, storage and networking without installing Azure command-line tools locally.
Microsoft maintains the Azure CLI and PowerShell modules in the hosted environment.
The shell uses your signed-in account and its existing permissions; opening a shell does not grant additional resource access.
Persist scripts and SSH keys in Cloud Shell storage so that they remain available between sessions.
Use the Cloud Shell editor to change stored scripts directly in the browser.

sections.title: A ready-made administration environment
paragraphs: Cloud Shell moves the command-line tools into a Microsoft-managed environment, so the browser is your access point rather than the machine doing the administration. Bash and PowerShell are alternative shell experiences. Choose the one that matches the script you need: an Azure CLI example uses az commands, while an Azure PowerShell example uses Az cmdlets. Keeping these examples in their intended shell makes quoting and variables easier to follow.

sections.title: Authentication does not add permission
paragraphs: Consider an engineer who can read a resource group but cannot change its virtual machines. Signing in through Cloud Shell makes the engineer’s account available to Azure tools; it does not promote the account to Contributor. The same distinction applies when moving between a managed workstation and a browser. A successful sign-in identifies the operator, while the account’s Azure permissions determine which resource operations are authorized.

sections.title: Choose how files survive
paragraphs: A troubleshooting script is useful only if you can find it during the next incident. Current Cloud Shell can run without attached storage, but files in that ephemeral session disappear when it closes. Mount storage when you need scripts or keys later. For a practical comparison, locate a saved script in CloudDrive, open it in the built-in editor, and distinguish that persistent file from the temporary running shell.

additionalSources.title: Microsoft Learn: use cloud shell editor

lessons.title: How does Azure Cloud Shell work?
points: Open Cloud Shell from shell.azure.com, the Azure portal or a supported Microsoft Learn code snippet.
A temporary host is allocated to your session; choose Bash or PowerShell before running commands.
Sessions terminate after 20 minutes of inactivity. Start a new session to continue working.
Files stored on CloudDrive persist after the temporary session ends and can be accessed from another device.
An Azure Files share can be mounted for persistent files; the share is associated with a particular region.
Open the built-in editor from the toolbar or run code <filename> to edit a file.
Cloud Shell includes tools such as Git, Terraform, Ansible, kubectl and Helm, alongside Azure tools.

sections.title: Follow the session lifecycle
paragraphs: Opening Cloud Shell allocates a temporary environment for your signed-in user. You can enter through the portal, its direct browser address, or supported documentation links. The environment is designed for interaction: twenty minutes without interactive activity ends the session. Starting another session restores access to persistent storage when configured, but does not resume the previous shell’s running processes or unsaved interactive state.

sections.title: Separate file storage from machine state
paragraphs: Suppose you edit a diagnostic script and set several Bash variables while investigating a VM. A saved script on mounted storage can be reused from another browser session. Those shell variables and the current process state belong to the temporary environment. Treat persistence as a file-storage capability, not a promise that the whole troubleshooting session becomes a durable virtual machine.

sections.title: Trace a reusable working session
paragraphs: Use a small text file to practise the boundary between editing, saving and reopening. The editor gives browser-based access to files, and Cloud Shell also includes common administration tools such as Git, kubectl and Terraform. Their presence avoids local installation for routine use; it does not make the environment an unrestricted machine for arbitrary privileged software.
steps: Choose Bash or PowerShell for the commands you intend to use.
Locate or create the practice file on your mounted CloudDrive and save changes in the editor.
Open a later session and verify the saved file is present before relying on it in a runbook.

additionalSources.title: Microsoft Learn: use cloud shell editor

lessons.title: When should you use Azure Cloud Shell?
points: Choose Cloud Shell for occasional Azure administration from a browser when your usual workstation is unavailable.
Use persistent storage when you need the same scripts in later sessions.
Avoid relying on a temporary shell session for unattended or long-running work; inactivity can disconnect the session and lose its current state.
Choose your own virtual machine or container when you need administrator privileges or unsupported installed tools.
Cloud Shell has a default limit of 20 concurrent users per tenant; request a quota increase for larger training sessions.

sections.title: Match the task to an interactive shell
paragraphs: Cloud Shell is well suited to an administrator who needs occasional command-line access while away from the usual workstation. For example, a browser session can provide the maintained Azure tools and an existing saved diagnostic script during an on-call investigation. The benefit is reducing setup on the borrowed device. The operator still needs the appropriate Azure account and resource permissions for the intended commands.

sections.title: Recognize the environment’s boundaries
paragraphs: The twenty-minute rule concerns inactivity, not a blanket ban on every command that lasts longer than twenty minutes. Nevertheless, an unattended workflow should not depend on an interactive session surviving. Cloud Shell users are unprivileged and cannot use sudo. When an installation requires elevated access or unsupported system changes, choose a suitable machine or container whose lifecycle and configuration you control.

sections.title: Plan persistence and shared usage
paragraphs: A team preparing a training event should consider both saved files and the tenant’s concurrent-user quota. Mounted storage keeps scripts available between sessions; an ephemeral session is appropriate when those files need not survive. Cloud Shell has a default limit of twenty concurrent users per tenant. A larger class should arrange a quota increase in advance, rather than interpreting a tenant quota error as a problem with an individual script.

lessons.title: Module assessment
points: Complete the interactive check on Microsoft Learn.

lessons.title: Summary
points: Use Cloud Shell for browser-based administration, and save files in persistent storage rather than relying on the temporary host.

modules.title: Deploy Azure infrastructure by using JSON ARM templates

lessons.title: Introduction
points: ARM templates describe Azure infrastructure declaratively in JSON and can be versioned with application code.
Microsoft recommends Bicep for people starting infrastructure as code on Azure because it offers simpler authoring than JSON templates.

lessons.title: Explore Azure Resource Manager template structure
points: Infrastructure as code keeps resource configuration in version control, making deployments repeatable and changes traceable.
An ARM template declares the desired resources and properties; Resource Manager organizes their creation and dependencies.
Templates are idempotent: repeating an unchanged deployment does not create duplicate resources.
The required template sections include $schema, contentVersion and resources. Optional sections include parameters, variables, functions and outputs.
Parameters supply deployment-specific values; variables simplify expressions; outputs return values after deployment.
Deploy a local template after signing in with az login or Connect-AzAccount and selecting the intended subscription and resource group.
For resource-group deployment, use az deployment group create or New-AzResourceGroupDeployment; review deployment status and history in the portal.

sections.title: Describe a target configuration
paragraphs: An ARM template records what a deployment should contain in JSON: resource types, names and properties, rather than a sequence of portal clicks. That makes configuration reviewable alongside application code. Resource Manager coordinates dependencies and can create independent resources in parallel. For example, a reviewed storage definition can be reused for several environments while the resource configuration remains traceable in version control.

sections.title: Read the template in layers
paragraphs: Start with $schema and contentVersion, which describe the document format and the version you assign to this template. Then inspect parameters for caller-supplied values, variables for reusable expressions, resources for deployed objects, and outputs for returned results. A resource’s type combines its provider and resource type, such as Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts. Its apiVersion selects the version of that resource’s deployment contract; it is different from contentVersion.

sections.title: Understand what repetition means
paragraphs: Idempotence means deploying the same desired configuration to the same resource identity does not create a duplicate merely because you rerun it. It does not mean an incomplete resource definition safely preserves every existing property. In incremental mode, define the resource’s complete intended non-default properties, because omitted properties can reset. Review the resulting deployment record and resource settings together; a successful deployment is evidence of execution, while those settings show the actual configuration.

lessons.title: Exercise - Create and deploy an Azure Resource Manager template
points: Create azuredeploy.json in Visual Studio Code with the template schema, version and an initially empty resources section.
Sign in using Azure CLI or PowerShell, select the intended subscription, and create or select the exercise resource group.
Deploy the empty template in the default incremental mode and inspect its successful deployment record; it creates no resources.
Add a Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts resource with its name, API version, location, kind and SKU, then deploy the updated template.
Review the resource and deployment history in the Azure portal. Follow the official exercise in your own chosen lab environment.

sections.title: Use an empty deployment to learn the workflow
paragraphs: Begin with a template that has an empty resources array. This separates learning the deployment process from learning a particular resource’s properties. In the default incremental mode, an empty template creates no resources while still giving you a deployment record to inspect. Its success demonstrates that the template was accepted at the selected scope; it does not prove that any later storage definition is valid.

sections.title: Make the deployment boundary explicit
paragraphs: Before adding storage, identify the subscription and lab resource group you intend to use. The template file supplies the resource definitions, while the command supplies the deployment scope. A deployment name labels the operation in history; it is not the storage account’s name. The example below explicitly supplies the resource group rather than depending on a previously configured CLI default.

code.text:
az deployment group create \
  --name storage-practice \
  --resource-group <lab-resource-group> \
  --template-file azuredeploy.json

sections.title: Compare the two deployment results
paragraphs: After the empty deployment, add a storage account resource with a valid name, API version, location, kind and SKU, then review the updated deployment. You should be able to explain why the first operation had no deployed resources and the second has storage. Keep the account’s resource settings and the deployment history in view, since they answer different questions: what exists now and which operation produced or updated it.
steps: Inspect the empty template’s resources array and deployment result.
Review every required storage resource property before the second deployment.
Locate the resulting storage account and compare its properties with the template.

lessons.title: Add flexibility to your Azure Resource Manager template by using parameters and outputs
points: Use parameters for values that vary by environment, such as resource names, SKUs, size and capacity.
Define each parameter with a type and optionally a default, allowed values, length or value constraints, and a description.
A template supports up to 256 parameters; supply values on the command line or in a parameter file.
Use secureString for secrets and secureObject for objects containing sensitive values. Do not hardcode secrets or provide secret defaults.
Reference a parameter in a resource with the parameters function, so one template can serve several environments.
Outputs have a declared type and value; the reference function can retrieve runtime resource properties such as storage endpoints.
Redeploying with the same resource names and scopes updates existing resources. In incremental mode, specify all non-default properties because omitted properties can reset to defaults.

sections.title: Parameterize genuine differences
paragraphs: A template becomes reusable when values that vary by environment are inputs instead of hardcoded resource properties. For example, development and production can supply different account names or supported redundancy SKUs to the same definition. A parameter’s type and constraints describe acceptable input. A default is used when the caller omits that value; allowedValues restricts what can be supplied and does not automatically choose a different entry from the list.

sections.title: Keep secrets out of ordinary values
paragraphs: Use secureString for a password or secret and secureObject for an object containing sensitive values. Do not place a secret directly in the template or give it a hardcoded default. Distinguish a resource name, which is useful deployment metadata, from credentials, which need protection. The parameter limit is 256 per template, so use inputs to represent configuration differences rather than recreating every constant as a parameter.

sections.title: Return useful results without changing input
paragraphs: An output exposes a value after deployment, such as the storage account’s service endpoints retrieved through reference. Outputs let another operation discover deployment results without copying a guessed endpoint into a script. They do not replace the parameters that determine the resource configuration. When redeploying with a changed input, keep the full intended resource definition: incremental mode reapplies properties and omitted values can revert to defaults.

lessons.title: Exercise - Add parameters and outputs to your Azure Resource Manager template
points: Add a storageName parameter and use it in the storage account resource name.
Add a storageSKU parameter with an allowedValues list and replace the fixed SKU with the parameter expression.
Deploy with an allowed SKU, then observe that a value outside the allowed list fails validation.
Add a storageEndpoint output using the storage account runtime properties and inspect it in the deployment result and portal.
Follow the official exercise for exact commands and naming requirements; this app does not deploy resources for you.

sections.title: Connect declarations to the resource
paragraphs: Defining storageName in the parameters section is only half the change. Replace the resource’s fixed name with the parameters function so deployment input actually affects the account. Apply the same principle to storageSKU: declare a default and supported allowed values, then use that parameter in the resource’s sku.name. A declared but unused parameter changes no resource property.

sections.title: Test a constraint deliberately
paragraphs: Imagine a deployment contract that permits Standard_LRS and Standard_GRS. Supplying Standard_GRS exercises a permitted alternative; supplying Basic should fail the declared allowed-values constraint. That comparison teaches the difference between choosing an input and validating it. Storage account names require global uniqueness and lowercase letters or numbers, with three to twenty-four characters. For example, a name like reportstore2026 follows the character pattern, but still needs an available globally unique name.

sections.title: Inspect the output contract
paragraphs: After deploying a permitted configuration, inspect both the resulting resource and the storageEndpoint output. The output uses the resource’s runtime primaryEndpoints object, so it reflects the deployed account rather than a manually composed string. The following fragment belongs in the template’s outputs section; it is not a complete template. Checking the object in deployment results helps connect the declared output type with its actual value.

lessons.title: Module assessment
points: Complete the interactive check on Microsoft Learn.

lessons.title: Summary
points: Parameters make a template reusable across deployments, while outputs expose useful results such as resource endpoints.

paths.title: AZ-104: Manage identities and governance in Azure

lessons.title: Introduction
points: Microsoft Entra ID is a cloud identity and access service for users, applications and devices.

lessons.title: Examine Microsoft Entra ID
points: Microsoft manages the Entra ID directory service; customers do not deploy or maintain its domain controllers.
Use Entra ID for users and groups, application access, single sign-on, multifactor authentication and Conditional Access.
A tenant is an isolated directory instance containing identities and applications.
An Azure subscription is associated with exactly one Entra tenant at a time; the same tenant can serve multiple subscriptions.
A tenant receives an onmicrosoft.com domain and can also use verified custom domain names.
Entra ID does not use the traditional organizational-unit and Group Policy hierarchy of AD DS.
An application object defines an application; a service principal represents that application in a particular tenant.

sections.title: Directory boundary and resource boundary
paragraphs: Think of a tenant as the directory that answers identity questions: which users, groups and applications exist, and how they authenticate. A subscription answers a different set of questions about Azure resources, access scope and billing. Connecting a subscription to a tenant lets identities from that directory receive Azure resource permissions. It does not give every directory member permission to administer the subscription. An organization can therefore keep one workforce directory while using separate subscriptions for development and production, with different resource permissions in each.

sections.title: Applications and organizational names
paragraphs: Each tenant starts with an onmicrosoft.com domain. A verified custom domain gives users an organizational sign-in name, but does not replace the tenant’s identity boundary. Application registration similarly creates an application definition rather than a resource subscription. A service principal represents that application inside a tenant where it is used. For example, a business application defined in one tenant can have a service principal in another tenant that authorizes its local use. Entra ID provides the cloud directory and identity features without asking the customer to build domain controllers or an OU hierarchy.

lessons.title: Compare Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory Domain Services
points: AD DS is a Windows Server directory with a hierarchical structure, organizational units, Group Policy and domain-joined computers.
AD DS uses LDAP for directory queries and Kerberos for authentication.
Entra ID is designed for internet applications and uses web protocols including SAML, OpenID Connect and OAuth.
Entra users and groups have a flat directory structure; traditional AD DS Group Policy does not apply to them.
Running an AD DS domain controller on an Azure virtual machine is distinct from using Entra ID.
The source recommends extra data disks for AD DS database, logs and SYSVOL on Azure virtual machines, with disk host caching set to None.

sections.title: Choose by the application’s expectations
paragraphs: An application built for AD DS might expect LDAP directory searches, Kerberos authentication and a computer joined to a Windows domain. AD DS also uses DNS to locate domain services and OUs to organize delegation and Group Policy. Moving its domain controller to an Azure VM changes where the server runs, not what directory technology it provides. You still operate the Windows Server and AD DS deployment. Entra ID is a separate cloud identity service, so simply having an Entra tenant does not supply that application with an LDAP domain controller.

sections.title: Modern identity and device management
paragraphs: For a web application, authentication can use protocols such as SAML or OpenID Connect, while OAuth handles authorization to protected APIs. These exchanges suit internet-based services without requiring traditional computer domain membership. Entra users and groups do not acquire AD DS Group Policy merely because their identities are in the cloud. For example, a company might retain AD DS for a legacy file application while using Entra ID for cloud application sign-in. If it deploys AD DS on Azure VMs, the module recommends separate data disks for the database, logs and SYSVOL, with host caching disabled for those disks.

lessons.title: Examine Microsoft Entra ID as a directory service for cloud apps
points: A shared Entra tenant can provide identity services for Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Intune.
Centralized application authentication can give users single sign-on across integrated cloud applications.
App Service authentication can use an Entra tenant to limit website access to accounts from that directory.
Deployment slots can use separate authentication settings.

sections.title: One directory across integrated services
paragraphs: Using a shared tenant avoids treating each Microsoft cloud application as a completely separate user directory. The same organizational identities can support Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Intune, with application integration providing single sign-on. This does not mean every user receives every application license or every resource permission. Identity establishes who the user is; the application and its access configuration determine what the user may do. A company can keep a consistent sign-in identity while giving different departments access to different integrated applications.

sections.title: Configure sign-in and authorization deliberately
paragraphs: App Service authentication can use an Entra app registration and tenant to validate incoming sign-in requests. Configure the app to require authentication when anonymous access is inappropriate, and choose a single-tenant or deliberately restricted tenant configuration for organizational access. Successful authentication alone is not always the complete authorization policy: by default, the associated tenant’s users may be able to access the application, so some applications need further access restrictions. Deployment slots can have separate authentication settings. A test slot should therefore be reviewed independently rather than assuming that production’s authentication configuration automatically describes its access behavior.

additionalSources.title: Microsoft Learn: configure authentication provider aad

lessons.title: Compare Microsoft Entra ID P1 and P2 plans
points: Entra ID premium editions add capabilities beyond the free directory features and require the relevant licenses.
P1 capabilities described here include Conditional Access, password reset with writeback, self-service group management and Connect Health.
P2 adds Identity Protection for risk-based account and sign-in protection.
P2 also adds Privileged Identity Management to control permanent and temporary privileged access through activation workflows.
Check current Microsoft licensing documentation before deciding which edition is required; plans and feature entitlements change.

sections.title: Translate a requirement into a feature
paragraphs: Start with the required identity control rather than treating premium licensing as a general Azure subscription upgrade. P1 adds capabilities such as Conditional Access, password reset with on-premises writeback and Connect Health. These solve different problems: an access policy can consider the sign-in context, while writeback lets an eligible cloud password reset update the on-premises directory. A company that needs those controls should identify the users benefiting from them and the package containing the required entitlement. Having paid Azure resource consumption does not by itself provide all premium Entra features.

sections.title: Risk protection and privileged activation
paragraphs: P2 includes Identity Protection capabilities for risk-based identity decisions and Privileged Identity Management. Identity Protection concerns risk associated with users and sign-ins; PIM concerns how privileged access is assigned and activated. For example, an administrator can be eligible for a privileged role and activate it through a controlled workflow when needed, instead of relying on standing administrative access for all work. These are distinct controls even when one licensing package includes both. Consult the current licensing tables before selecting a package, because bundles and the entitlements of adjacent governance products can differ.

lessons.title: Examine Microsoft Entra Domain Services
points: Entra Domain Services provides managed domain capabilities for workloads needing domain join, Group Policy or traditional authentication.
It can support applications using LDAP, NTLM or Kerberos without you operating the domain controllers.
An alternative is to connect to on-premises domain controllers over a VPN or run AD DS domain controllers on Azure virtual machines.
With on-premises directory integration, users can use organizational identities across local and cloud environments.
The managed service reduces domain-controller maintenance and replication administration, but has service-specific limitations and usage charges.

sections.title: Managed domain services for legacy workloads
paragraphs: Entra Domain Services supplies familiar domain capabilities such as domain join, Group Policy, LDAP and Kerberos or NTLM authentication, while Microsoft operates the domain controllers. This is useful when an application cannot be changed to use modern cloud identity protocols. Compare it with two alternatives: connecting Azure workloads to on-premises domain controllers over a VPN, or deploying and maintaining AD DS replicas on Azure VMs. The managed service reduces domain-controller operation, but it is still a specific managed domain with its own supported administration model and consumption charges.

sections.title: Understand the synchronization direction
paragraphs: Directory identities and credentials synchronize from Entra ID into the managed domain; this is not a two-way replacement for the source directory. Existing synchronized users and groups should be managed at their source rather than edited in the managed domain. Traditional authentication also requires the appropriate Kerberos and NTLM password hashes. Cloud users may need to change or reset their password before those hashes exist, while hybrid deployments need the corresponding password-hash synchronization configuration. For example, a successful cloud sign-in alone does not prove that an older user account is already ready to authenticate to the managed domain.

lessons.title: Module assessment
points: Complete the interactive check on Microsoft Learn.

lessons.title: Summary
points: Entra ID serves cloud identity needs, AD DS provides traditional domain services, and managed Entra Domain Services supports suitable legacy application requirements.

lessons.title: Introduction
points: Manage user identities, groups, licensing and device registration centrally, giving people only the access needed for their work.

lessons.title: Create, configure, and manage users
points: Manage user objects under Identity, Users, All users in the Entra admin center; switch directory before changing another tenant.
Cloud identities are managed in Entra ID; directory-synchronized identities originate in on-premises Active Directory.
Guest accounts represent people outside the organization, such as contractors, and their access should be removed when no longer needed.
Cloud Sync uses lightweight agents with cloud-managed synchronization; choose Cloud Sync or Connect Sync after comparing the capabilities your deployment requires.
User type and source help distinguish tenant members, invited guests and synchronized accounts.

sections.title: Identify where an account is maintained
paragraphs: Before changing a user, identify the tenant and the account’s source. A cloud-managed account is maintained in Entra ID, whereas a directory-synchronized identity originates in an on-premises directory and reaches Entra ID through synchronization. External access is another dimension: a guest represents someone invited into the organization’s directory for collaboration. User type and source help interpret these differences, but they are not a substitute for checking the account’s actual access. In a company with several directories, switching to the intended tenant is an essential first step before editing users or reviewing membership.

sections.title: Plan identity lifecycle and synchronization
paragraphs: For example, a contractor may need an invited identity for the duration of a project, while a permanent employee already has an account in the company’s on-premises AD. These cases should not automatically receive the same creation or maintenance process. Remove external access when it is no longer needed and keep synchronized identity changes connected to the authoritative directory. Cloud Sync uses cloud-managed configuration and lightweight agents; current capabilities include device synchronization when enabled. Compare it with Connect Sync against the requirements of the deployment, rather than assuming the two tools always have identical features or that the older training comparison defines today’s limits.

additionalSources.title: Microsoft Learn: what is cloud sync

lessons.title: Exercise - assign licenses to users
points: Use a tenant where you have the required user-administration permissions to create a test user.
Create an assigned security group and add the test user as a member, with an administrator as its owner.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open Billing, Licenses, select a product, choose Groups and assign the license to the group.
Verify the group assignment and the resulting license on the test user.

sections.title: Prepare identities before assigning products
paragraphs: This exercise combines user creation, security-group membership and licensing. Use an appropriate tenant with permission to administer its users and groups, plus an available product that can be assigned for the test. Create a recognizable test account, set its usage location and place it directly in an assigned security group. Choose an owner who can maintain the group’s membership. The group is the vehicle for the license policy; creating the group alone does not give its users a product entitlement. Keep the account and group identifiable so the assignment and later cleanup can be checked without affecting unrelated users.

sections.title: Trace the inherited license to the user
paragraphs: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, use Billing and Licenses to choose the product and assign it to the group. A supported licensing role, such as License Administrator, is needed for that stage. Review which service plans are enabled, because one product may include several services. Then inspect the group’s processing result and the test user’s effective license state. A successful configuration on the group does not mean every member immediately received a usable license: insufficient capacity or a user-specific error can still prevent assignment. Group-based licensing does not expand nested group membership, so use direct user membership for this straightforward exercise.

lessons.title: Exercise - restore or remove deleted users
points: Select a test account in Entra Users and delete it, then open Deleted users to find the suspended account.
Deleted user accounts can be restored during the 30-day retention window.
Choose Restore user, confirm the operation, and verify that the account appears again under All users.
Permanent deletion cannot be undone; use the official lab instructions and required administrator role.

sections.title: Deletion has a recovery window
paragraphs: Deleting a user moves the account into Deleted users rather than immediately removing every possibility of recovery. The normal retention window is 30 days. During that period, an appropriately authorized administrator can restore a user that has not been permanently deleted. After the window expires, permanent deletion begins; deliberately permanently deleting the account also removes the restore option. This distinction matters when investigating an accidental deletion. Finding an account under Deleted users means that a restore operation may still be available, not that the user can continue signing in as though nothing happened.

sections.title: Check recovery using a test identity
paragraphs: Use a clearly identified test account and verify the tenant before selecting Delete user. After deletion, open Deleted users and confirm that the correct account appears. Select Restore user, confirm the operation and return to All users to verify that the restored identity is present. Review the restored account’s properties and the access or licensing relevant to the exercise, rather than treating the presence of its name as the only useful check. For example, an accidental deletion discovered after ten days belongs in this recovery process; recreating a new account is a different operation and should not be confused with restoring the original object.

lessons.title: Create, configure, and manage groups
points: Use security groups to manage access to shared resources; members can include users, devices and service principals.
Use Microsoft 365 groups for collaboration resources such as shared mailboxes, calendars, files and SharePoint sites.
Assigned membership is maintained manually. Dynamic membership adds or removes members according to attribute-based rules.
Dynamic user membership works with security and Microsoft 365 groups; dynamic device membership applies only to security groups.
A change such as a user moving department can change their dynamic group memberships automatically.
Dynamic user groups require enough Entra ID P1 or Intune for Education licenses for every unique user member; dynamic device group members need no license.

sections.title: Match the group to its purpose
paragraphs: Security groups collect identities that should receive shared access to resources; their members can include users, devices and service principals. Microsoft 365 groups instead support a collaboration experience with a shared mailbox, calendar, files and a SharePoint site. These choices are not just different labels for the same object. For example, a group representing devices subject to an access rule belongs in a security-group design, while a sales team needing a shared collaboration workspace may fit a Microsoft 365 group. Select the group’s purpose before deciding how its membership will be maintained.

sections.title: Keep rules and entitlements aligned
paragraphs: Assigned membership is useful when an owner should explicitly choose each member. Dynamic user membership is useful when an attribute, such as Department, should determine inclusion automatically. Changing that attribute can then add or remove the user as rules are processed. Dynamic device membership evaluates device attributes and applies to security groups, not Microsoft 365 groups. Current product guidance requires enough P1 or Intune for Education licenses for unique users in dynamic user groups, but no member licenses for devices in dynamic device groups. Because attribute changes can affect access, consider who is allowed to modify the attributes used by a rule.

lessons.title: Exercise - add groups in Microsoft Entra ID
points: In Entra Identity, Groups, create a Microsoft 365 group with Assigned membership.
Choose an owner and members, then verify the new group in All groups after refreshing if necessary.
Follow the official exercise in a tenant where you have the required user-administration permissions.

sections.title: Define the collaboration boundary
paragraphs: This exercise creates a Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership. Choose that group type because its purpose is collaboration, not because every group is interchangeable. Assigned membership means that owners or administrators maintain the chosen members rather than relying on attribute-based dynamic rules. Decide which people should collaborate before creating the group, and give it a name that explains the team it represents. An owner has responsibility for maintaining the group; being its owner is distinct from simply appearing in the member list. The lab assigns an administrator as owner and selects a member explicitly.

sections.title: Verify the object and its membership
paragraphs: In the intended Entra tenant, open Groups, create the Microsoft 365 group and choose Assigned membership. Select the owner and the intended user members before completing creation. Refresh All groups if the new object is not yet visible, then inspect the group rather than relying solely on the creation notification. Check that the type, membership model, owner and members match the intended collaboration team. For example, a manually maintained regional sales team should not accidentally become a dynamic device group. This exercise establishes the group object and membership; it is separate from granting Azure resource roles or configuring a product license policy.

lessons.title: Configure and manage device registration
points: Entra registered devices support personal-device and mobile scenarios; users can keep local device sign-in while adding a work account.
Entra joined devices use an organizational account for device sign-in and suit cloud-first management.
Hybrid Entra joined devices remain joined to on-premises AD DS and also have an Entra device identity.
Use hybrid join when existing applications require AD machine authentication or devices must retain Group Policy and existing imaging processes.
Device identity can support Conditional Access; Intune or another management tool applies compliance and security settings.
Entra join supports Windows 10 and Windows 11 except Home editions; check current support before choosing other operating systems.
Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust enables on-premises authentication from Entra joined or hybrid joined devices after Microsoft Entra Kerberos and the required policies are configured.

sections.title: Registration and join solve different problems
paragraphs: Device identity describes a device’s relationship with the directory; management tools then apply configuration and compliance controls. An Entra registered personal device can keep its normal local sign-in while adding a work account for organizational access. An Entra joined organizational Windows device uses the organizational account for device sign-in and fits cloud-oriented management. A hybrid joined device remains joined to on-premises AD DS and also has an Entra identity. For example, retaining existing AD machine authentication and Group Policy can justify hybrid join, whereas a personal laptop used for work applications may fit registration.

sections.title: Combine identity, compliance and authentication
paragraphs: Conditional Access can use device information, but merely creating a device identity is not the same as applying security configurations. Intune or another management system supplies the compliance and configuration controls used by the organization. Check the supported operating systems and editions before selecting a join approach; Windows Home is not included in the Windows Entra-join support described here. For Windows Hello for Business in suitable hybrid environments, cloud Kerberos trust uses Microsoft Entra Kerberos and required policies to enable on-premises authentication. It is a specific passwordless authentication design, not a claim that all historical device-writeback scenarios have the same replacement.

lessons.title: Manage licenses
points: Assign user service licenses through the Microsoft 365 admin center or supported administration APIs and tools.
Group-based licensing assigns product licenses to members automatically and removes inherited licenses when members leave.
Provide enough licenses for each unique member who needs the licensed product and meet the group-based licensing entitlement requirements.
A product license can have selected service plans disabled when a service is not required.
The same product assigned through multiple groups or both directly and through a group consumes one license for that user.
Set each user’s correct usage location before assignment because some services are not available in every location.
Investigate assignment errors such as insufficient licenses or conflicting services rather than assuming every group member was licensed successfully.

sections.title: Separate the product from its service plans
paragraphs: A product license can contain several service plans. Assigning the product while disabling a particular plan lets an organization adopt its services in stages. For example, a department can receive its required productivity product while a service it is not ready to use remains disabled. Licensing is managed through the Microsoft 365 admin center or supported administration tools and APIs, while Entra ID stores users’ license assignment state. Set each user’s correct usage location because service availability can depend on location; a tenant-wide default may not accurately describe a geographically distributed workforce.

sections.title: Understand effective licenses and background processing
paragraphs: Group-based licensing applies the group’s products to its user members and reacts to membership changes. A user can receive the same product directly and through multiple groups, but that product consumes one license for that user rather than one for every assignment path. The effective service state combines the applicable assignments. This also means removing one path does not necessarily remove every entitlement. Check processing errors and available license capacity instead of assuming group configuration guarantees success. Group-based licensing does not traverse nested groups, so users hidden inside a child group are not automatically licensed by the parent assignment.

lessons.title: Exercise - change group license assignments
points: Review the group’s current license assignments, then change them under Billing, Licenses in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Check processing results and user error states after the assignment; group licensing runs in the background.
Resolve insufficient licenses, conflicting service plans, missing prerequisites, unsupported usage locations or duplicate proxy addresses as applicable.
For an add-on product, assign its prerequisite service plan together with the add-on in the licensing group.
When migrating direct licenses to group assignments, first assign equivalent group licenses and verify success before removing the direct assignments.
Check a subset of users and audit logs during migration so that users do not lose services or data.
After correcting a license problem, trigger supported reprocessing where needed and verify that the user’s resulting license state is correct.

sections.title: Diagnose the error before changing assignments
paragraphs: Group licensing runs in the background, so a user can enter an error state even though the administrator’s intention to assign a product remains recorded. Inspect the affected users and the reported error before choosing a fix. Insufficient licenses require available capacity; conflicting service plans require resolving the overlap; dependency errors require retaining the prerequisite or removing the dependent service. An unsupported usage location is not fixed by repeatedly retrying an unchanged assignment. Duplicate proxy addresses can also prevent successful processing. Correct the underlying data or assignment, then use supported reprocessing where necessary and verify the resulting license state.

sections.title: Migrate without creating a license gap
paragraphs: A safe migration preserves the services a user already has until the replacement assignment has succeeded. Create or select the new licensing group, add the intended users and assign equivalent products and service plans. Check the group’s processing status, audit records and representative user details before gradually removing the direct assignments. The same product assigned both directly and through a group is consumed once, so this overlap need not double that user’s license consumption. Moving between licensed groups follows the same principle: add to the destination and confirm its license before removing from the source. For add-ons, keep the required prerequisite plans in the licensing group.

lessons.title: Exercise - change user license assignments
points: Create a test user in Entra ID and set the user’s usage location.
In Microsoft 365 Billing, Licenses, choose a product and use Assign licenses for the test account.
Verify the result on the user’s Licenses page in the Entra admin center.

sections.title: Prepare the individual assignment
paragraphs: Create a test user in the correct Entra tenant and set a real, appropriate usage location. That property influences whether a service may be assigned and used; it is not simply a label for the preferred Azure region. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, choose the product under Billing and Licenses, open the licensed-user view and assign it to the intended account. Use a supported role such as License Administrator. Review which services within the product are enabled, because changing a product assignment can affect more than one application available to the user.

sections.title: Inspect the user’s resulting state
paragraphs: After assignment, verify the product on the user’s license view and check for any errors rather than stopping at the assign action. Distinguish a direct assignment made here from a license inherited through a group. A user might already have the same product through a group, in which case the additional assignment path does not consume a second copy of that product. Likewise, removing the direct assignment would not necessarily remove an inherited entitlement. For example, a lab user who remains in a product-licensed group can continue to have that product after its direct assignment is removed. Inspect the effective assignments when explaining the result.

lessons.title: Create custom security attributes
points: Custom security attributes are tenant-wide business-specific key-value pairs assigned to users or enterprise applications.
Use them to categorize identities and applications or support fine-grained resource-access decisions.
Attribute types are Boolean, integer and string. Integer and string attributes can allow multiple values or predefined choices; Boolean attributes are single-valued.
Attributes can also be assigned to users synchronized from on-premises AD.
The source states that custom security attributes are not supported in Entra Domain Services, SAML token claims or JWT claims.

sections.title: Design attributes with useful types
paragraphs: Custom security attributes provide business-specific information on supported directory objects, including users and enterprise applications. Organize related definitions into attribute sets, and choose types according to how the information will be used. A Boolean attribute answers a yes-or-no question; an integer can represent a numerical category; a string can identify a project. Integer and string attributes can support multiple values or predefined choices, while Boolean attributes remain single-valued. For example, a project list assigned to an application can support inventory filtering, and a project identifier assigned to a user can contribute to a supported resource-access condition.

sections.title: Separate definition from assignment permissions
paragraphs: Attribute governance is important when the values influence access or contain sensitive business information. Defining the schema and assigning values are separate administrative responsibilities, with dedicated attribute roles that can be scoped to the tenant or an attribute set. Global Administrator does not automatically receive permission to read, define or assign these attributes. This allows a department to maintain its own attributes without opening every attribute set to it. Custom security attributes can be assigned to directory-synchronized users, but they are not a general-purpose extension of every downstream directory or token: current documentation does not support them in Domain Services, SAML token claims or JWT claims.

lessons.title: Explore automatic user creation
points: SCIM is an open standard for exchanging identity information and automating user and group provisioning.
The Entra provisioning service connects to a target application’s SCIM endpoint using its schema and REST APIs.
An authoritative HR system can drive creation, attribute updates and deprovisioning as employees join, change roles or leave.
API-driven inbound provisioning supports sources that do not expose a SCIM endpoint by accepting workforce data from an automation tool or script.
Keep provisioning and deprovisioning connected to the identity lifecycle so that departed employees do not retain unnecessary access.

sections.title: Connect provisioning to the employee lifecycle
paragraphs: Authentication and provisioning answer different questions. Authentication verifies a sign-in; provisioning creates, updates or removes the accounts and attributes needed in an application or directory. SCIM standardizes the exchange of identity information through a schema and REST interfaces. The Entra provisioning service can connect to a target application’s SCIM endpoint to automate user and group changes. For example, an authoritative HR record can drive account creation when an employee joins, an attribute update after a role change and deprovisioning when employment ends. The value comes from keeping entitlement changes connected to those lifecycle events rather than relying on a separate manual checklist for every system.

sections.title: Handle sources without a native SCIM endpoint
paragraphs: An HR system does not need to expose the exact target interface itself for every inbound scenario. API-driven inbound provisioning accepts workforce information collected by an automation tool or script from an authoritative source. The source data and integration therefore determine the lifecycle changes, while the provisioning service processes those changes for the destination. Distinguish the authoritative HR system, the Entra identity repository and a target application when planning the flow. A successful application sign-in does not prove that its provisioning integration also removes accounts correctly. Review creation, updates and departure handling as separate parts of the same identity lifecycle.

points: User lifecycle, group membership, licensing and device identity work together to control access and keep organizational identities current.

modules.title: Describe the core architectural components of Azure

lessons.title: Introduction
points: Azure has a physical structure of datacenters, zones and regions, alongside a management hierarchy for resources, access and billing.

lessons.title: What is Microsoft Azure
points: Azure provides cloud services ranging from virtual machines and storage to managed databases and web applications.
Move an existing workload to virtual machines or modernize parts of it using managed services.
Scale resources up or out when demand rises and reduce them when demand falls to avoid unnecessary unused capacity.

sections.title: Choose how much infrastructure to operate
paragraphs: Azure offers both infrastructure services and managed application services. Moving an existing application to a VM is a practical starting point when it needs a familiar operating system and server environment. Modernizing the workload can change that operational model: a managed database reduces the need to run the database server yourself, and a managed app platform can handle parts of application hosting. These approaches can coexist. For example, an organization can keep its application on VMs initially while moving its data tier to a managed service, rather than trying to redesign every component at once.

sections.title: Relate capacity to actual demand
paragraphs: A cloud deployment should account for how the workload’s demand changes. Scaling up changes the capacity of an instance, while scaling out adds instances where the service and application support it. During a seasonal demand increase, additional capacity can help maintain service; after demand falls, reducing unnecessary capacity can avoid paying for resources no longer needed. Selecting Azure alone does not explain which scaling approach an application can use, so consider its hosting model and operational needs. Central monitoring helps the team judge health and demand rather than leaving a larger configuration running indefinitely after a temporary spike.

lessons.title: Get started with Azure accounts
points: An Azure subscription is required to create and use Azure resources.
An account can have several subscriptions, allowing development, testing and production workloads to be separated.
Free and student offers have service limits and time-limited credits; check the current offer before relying on it.
When practicing in Azure, monitor usage and remove resources that are no longer needed to avoid unexpected costs.

sections.title: Accounts and subscriptions have different roles
paragraphs: An Azure account provides the identity used to sign in, while a subscription provides access to Azure products and a boundary for creating and billing resources. The same account can be associated with more than one subscription. For example, an administrator can use one identity while keeping development resources in a different subscription from production. Check the selected subscription before following a lab, because signing in successfully does not guarantee that the tools or portal are currently targeting the subscription intended for the exercise. Resource creation and cost tracking belong to that selected subscription’s context.

sections.title: Understand a free offer before using it
paragraphs: Free account and student offers combine limited free services with credits that apply for specified periods. They are not promises that every Azure resource is free indefinitely. The standard free account uses payment details for identity verification and requires an upgrade before charging for continued paid use; the student offer can be obtained without a credit card when its eligibility requirements are met. Check the current offer’s included services, credit period and limits before planning a lab. Monitor actual usage and remove resources after practice, especially after moving to a paid subscription, rather than assuming a resource remains free because it was created during an introductory offer.

lessons.title: Describe Azure physical infrastructure
points: A region groups nearby datacenters connected by low-latency networking. Choose a suitable region for regional resource deployments.
Service availability, virtual machine sizes and storage features differ by region; some services such as Entra ID and Azure DNS are global.
Availability zones are physically separate datacenter groups within a region, each with independent power, cooling and networking.
A zonal resource is placed in a selected zone, while a zone-redundant service replicates across zones. Not every region or service supports zones.
Region pairs can support resilience across a geography, but not every region has a traditional pair.
Do not assume regional failover or replication is automatic: individual services may require customer configuration.
Sovereign Azure environments are isolated from the main Azure environment to meet particular legal or compliance requirements.

sections.title: Pick the region and the resilience boundary
paragraphs: A region groups nearby datacenters connected by low-latency networking. Selecting it affects where a regional workload runs and which service capabilities are available. Availability zones provide separate power, cooling and networking boundaries inside a supported region. A zonal deployment pins a resource to one selected zone; a zone-redundant service handles replication or distribution across zones. For example, putting two VMs in the same zone does not create the same physical isolation as placing them in separate zones. First confirm support for the service and region, then choose the configuration that matches the workload’s resilience requirements.

sections.title: Plan beyond one region deliberately
paragraphs: Zone resilience addresses failures within a region, but a sufficiently broad incident can affect the whole region. Cross-region recovery is a different design decision. A region pair may support service recovery planning, yet not every region has a traditional pair and not every service automatically replicates or fails over to it. Review the individual service’s recovery configuration instead of relying on the pair’s existence. Also distinguish global services, such as Azure DNS and Entra ID, from resources requiring a regional placement. Sovereign Azure environments provide isolated instances for particular legal or compliance requirements; choosing one is a different decision from choosing two ordinary regions for redundancy.

lessons.title: Describe Azure management infrastructure
points: The management hierarchy is management group, subscription, resource group and resource.

A resource group contains resource-group-scoped resources; each belongs to one group at a time. Some resources, such as policy definitions, exist at subscription or management-group scope. Groups cannot be nested or renamed.
Deleting a resource group deletes the resources it contains, so group resources with an appropriate shared lifecycle.
A subscription is a billing and access-management boundary; separate subscriptions can isolate environments, teams or cost reporting.
Management groups organize multiple subscriptions so that governance and access settings can apply across them.
Azure RBAC assignments and Azure Policy assignments at parent scopes apply to child scopes, including subscriptions and their resources.
A tenant has a Tenant Root Group. Management groups can be nested up to six levels, excluding the root and subscription levels; each group or subscription has one parent.

sections.title: Group resources by lifecycle and ownership
paragraphs: Resource groups provide a useful lifecycle boundary for resource-group-scoped objects. A temporary environment can keep its VMs, network and storage in one group so cleanup removes that environment together. Production resources that must remain should not be mixed into a disposable group. A group cannot be nested or renamed, and a resource-group-scoped resource belongs to one group at a time. Some Azure resource types instead exist at subscription or management-group scope. Naming and grouping should therefore reflect the intended ownership and lifecycle without assuming every object in Azure must be inside an ordinary resource group.

sections.title: Scale governance above a single subscription
paragraphs: Subscriptions separate billing and access-management contexts, while management groups organize subscriptions under a shared governance hierarchy. For example, a production management group can carry a location policy used by all its subscriptions, while development subscriptions sit elsewhere in the hierarchy. Azure RBAC and Azure Policy assignments apply through their scopes; this does not mean every resource property or label universally inherits from a parent. Each management group or subscription has one parent, and the management-group hierarchy supports six levels below the tenant root, excluding subscription levels. Plan shared assignments at the appropriate ancestor instead of repeating equivalent configuration independently in every subscription.
